newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The finance ministry is establishing a new criminal code for tax crimes and violations, in legislation shortly to be submitted to parliament. The code aims at rationalising revenues from fines and making the system simpler and more effective.

--The US, through its ambassador to Athens Thomas Niles, is attempting to encourage Greek and Turkish joint ventures in third countries, beginning with Russia, in the hope that cooperation in the business field will lay the ground for cooperation between Athens and Ankara.

--Four years in the making, the new legislation on the national health system will be submitted to parliament at the end of the month. Major changes have been made to outpatient care, operation of hospitals and labour relations for hospital doctors.
--Bank employees and electricity workers have rejected proposed wage increases and left open the prospect of strike action.
--Greece pledges 20 billion drachmas to Albania as it ponders the problems involved in a resignation of Albanian President Sali Berisha and participation in an international police force.
--The education ministry is expected to reply today to teachers' alternate proposals to making up for time lost over the eight-week strike.

--The war of words continues between Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel: yesterday the German foreign ministry responded ironically to Pangalos's statements regarding Germany's policies on Monday. Later in Thessaloniki, Pangalos said he was "tired of receiving lessons from unworthy representatives of countries unable to deal with their own problems".
--The finance ministry is tightening the noose on property owners with plans to establish a special service to monitor all property transactions electronically as of next year.

--Costas Karamanlis is confident he will win the leadership of the conservation opposition New Democracy party on Friday: "I will win and unite ND," he says. "All cadres will be used in a new beginning".

--Two Eleftheros Typos journalists today will testify in their defence after being charged with "espionage" over their reports on backstage negotiations between the governments in Athens and Skopje over a compromise on the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia's name.
--Some 500 state services face merger or abolition, in line with plans to rationalise and cut back costs in the public sector. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
